subject.title: Dashboard /compact silently wipes context once Claude CLI session is over the 1M cap

question: For ordinary Claude CLI sessions already near or over the native context cap, what should OpenClaw promise when Dashboard `/compact` is requested?
rationale: The current source intentionally delegates ordinary Claude CLI compaction to Claude Code, and the remaining choices affect session-state ownership, native transcript access, user recovery UX, and compatibility with Claude Code resume behavior.

options.title: Fail Loudly With Recovery Guidance
options.body: Keep Claude CLI compaction backend-owned for now, but make Dashboard and run-loop recovery refuse with clear export/manual-prune guidance and never rotate or checkpoint empty context.

options.title: Delegate Fully To Claude Code
options.body: Close this only after maintainers obtain live proof that native Claude Code compaction preserves resumable context past the cap and can surface a trustworthy status/result to OpenClaw.

options.title: Build OpenClaw Fallback Recovery
options.body: Implement a tested OpenClaw-owned over-cap path that reads the native Claude transcript or uses a fallback summarizer before any session rotation.

recommendation.title: Fail Loudly With Recovery Guidance
recommendation.body: Keep Claude CLI compaction backend-owned for now, but make Dashboard and run-loop recovery refuse with clear export/manual-prune guidance and never rotate or checkpoint empty context.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the native compaction ownership contract that determines the current Claude CLI deferral boundary.
